title: Validate Transfer username before inspect or mutation
description: Follow-up from the slskd-cli-9ps code review. slskd 0.26.1 looks up GET and DELETE downloads by Transfer ID even though the route includes username. src/transfer.ts trusts the response without checking its username, so a wrong username paired with a valid ID can inspect, cancel, or delete another user Transfer. Validate the returned Transfer username before any result or mutation and cover mismatched routes at the packaged CLI boundary.
acceptance_criteria: A mismatched username and valid Transfer ID returns a typed error; no DELETE request is sent for cancel or delete; matching references still work.

title: Verify and document the packaged Workflow
description:
## Parent
slskd-cli-9ps

## What to build
A trusted user can install the published package contract and follow documented commands and JSON results to create a Search, inspect Candidates, explicitly enqueue one, observe completion, and resume observation in a separate process. The complete Workflow is verified through the packaged executable.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A representative command-boundary test covers Search creation, Candidate inspection, explicit enqueue, completion, and resumed observation in another process without CLI Workflow state.
- [ ] The npm executable and exact supported Node.js range pass the release gate.
- [ ] Documentation covers installation, Connection profile precedence, command contracts, JSON result shapes, exit codes, acknowledgements, Search expiry, safe retry and reconciliation, and Transfer completion limits.
- [ ] Documented examples match the executable behavior.
close_reason: Implemented and validated at the packaged CLI boundary; remaining upstream API gaps are tracked in .1 and .5.

title: Clear and delete Transfers with explicit acknowledgement
description:
## Parent
slskd-cli-9ps

## What to build
A calling agent can explicitly clear or delete a slskd Transfer record. Each state-changing command requires its own literal --yes; slskd retains authority for download placement and file deletion.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Clearing and deletion each require --yes and make no state-changing request when it is absent.
- [ ] Each command reports deterministic JSON and stable exit codes for success, invalid input, missing Transfer, remote failure, and ambiguous outcome.
- [ ] The CLI does not move, remove, or verify downloaded files.
- [ ] Packaged command-boundary tests verify each operation and acknowledgement independently.
close_reason: Implemented and validated at the packaged CLI boundary; remaining upstream API gaps are tracked in .1 and .5.

title: Safely enqueue an explicitly selected Candidate
description:
## Parent
slskd-cli-9ps

## What to build
A calling agent enqueues only the Candidate it selected by Search and Candidate identifiers, with a literal --yes acknowledgement. The command validates the inspected association and Search lifetime, reconciles existing matching slskd Transfers before a safe retry, and reports an Ambiguous mutation when a network outcome is unknown.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Missing --yes causes no state-changing request and returns a documented JSON error and exit code.
- [ ] Invalid, mismatched, missing, or stale Candidate references are rejected without enqueuing.
- [ ] A valid selection creates the intended slskd Transfer and returns an inspectable Transfer reference.
- [ ] A safe retry reports an existing matching Transfer without creating a duplicate.
- [ ] Unknown mutation outcomes are reported as Ambiguous mutation; the CLI does not automatically retry the state-changing request.
- [ ] Packaged command-boundary tests assert the selected target, mutation count, retry reconciliation, and ambiguous outcome.
close_reason: Implemented and validated at the packaged CLI boundary; remaining upstream API gaps are tracked in .1 and .5.

title: Cancel a Transfer idempotently
description:
## Parent
slskd-cli-9ps

## What to build
A calling agent cancels a Transfer with a literal --yes acknowledgement and gets a convergent result when the Transfer is already cancelled or completed.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Missing --yes causes no state-changing request.
- [ ] Active Transfer cancellation reports the resulting slskd state in deterministic JSON.
- [ ] Already-cancelled and completed Transfers are reported as unchanged terminal resources.
- [ ] Unknown mutation outcomes are surfaced as Ambiguous mutation rather than automatically retried.
- [ ] Packaged command-boundary tests verify acknowledgement, idempotence, output, and exit codes.
close_reason: Implemented and validated at the packaged CLI boundary; remaining upstream API gaps are tracked in .1 and .5.

title: Observe slskd Transfer state and destination
description:
## Parent
slskd-cli-9ps

## What to build
A calling agent inspects an existing Transfer through slskd, sees queueing, progress, failure, completion, and its reported Transfer destination, and can resume observation from a separate CLI process. slskd's completed status is the Workflow completion authority.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Transfer inspection reports slskd state, progress when available, terminal status, and reported destination in deterministic JSON.
- [ ] A completed Transfer is reported as complete without claiming local file verification.
- [ ] Observation works in a fresh process without a CLI Workflow-run database or other persisted Transfer state.
- [ ] Missing Transfer and remote failures have documented JSON errors and stable exit codes.
- [ ] Packaged command-boundary tests cover active, failed, and completed Transfers.
notes:
Fixture tests now cover queued, active, failed, completed, and cancelled Transfer states. Live slskd currently has zero Transfer records, so live observation could not be exercised. slskd 0.26.1 Transfer response has no actual destination field. GET /options exposes a configured download root but no per-Transfer resolved path; CLI leaves destination:null rather than inventing one.
2026-10-17: User accepted the slskd 0.26.1 limitation. The documented public contract returns destination:null when the per-Transfer resolved path is unavailable; slskd completion remains authoritative.
close_reason: Transfer observation implemented and tested; user accepted the documented upstream destination limitation.

title: Inspect Search Candidates with scoped identifiers
description:
## Parent
slskd-cli-9ps

## What to build
A calling agent inspects Candidates for a Search before making a selection. Each Candidate has an opaque identifier scoped to its Search and normalized Candidate metadata; unavailable information is represented explicitly. An Expired search is rejected so the agent can create a fresh Search.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Candidates are associated with their Search identifier and have stable opaque Candidate identifiers usable for explicit selection.
- [ ] Metadata includes source username, remote path, filename, extension, byte size, available queue or slot information, and parsed audio attributes when exposed by slskd.
- [ ] Unavailable metadata is explicit, with no invented values or automatic ranking.
- [ ] Missing and Expired search references return distinct documented JSON errors and exit codes.
- [ ] Packaged command-boundary tests verify response normalization and expiry behavior.
close_reason: Implemented and validated at the packaged CLI boundary; remaining upstream API gaps are tracked in .1 and .5.

title: Create a bounded Search from a literal query
description:
## Parent
slskd-cli-9ps

## What to build
A calling agent creates a slskd-backed Search from one literal free-text Search query and receives a Search identifier for later inspection. The lifetime is bounded, defaults to 60 seconds, and can be configured within documented limits.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The CLI passes the supplied Search query unchanged, without inferred filters, ranking, or automatic selection.
- [ ] Successful output contains the Search identifier and lifetime in deterministic JSON.
- [ ] Invalid query and lifetime inputs return documented JSON errors and stable exit codes.
- [ ] Packaged command-boundary tests assert the slskd request and output.
close_reason: Implemented and validated at the packaged CLI boundary; remaining upstream API gaps are tracked in .1 and .5.

title: Set up and verify the agent-first CLI connection
description:
## Parent
slskd-cli-9ps

## What to build
A trusted user can install and run the TypeScript npm package as slskd-cli, configure one Connection profile, and verify that it reaches a compatible slskd instance. This first slice establishes the executable, build and test commands, and a controllable slskd HTTP fixture for command-boundary tests. The CLI resolves TOML profile values, then environment variables, then flags, and produces deterministic, non-interactive JSON with stable exit codes.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The npm package exposes a working slskd-cli executable on the documented supported Node.js range, with reproducible build and test commands.
- [ ] A command verifies a configured slskd instance at version 0.26.1 or later and distinguishes incompatible version, authentication, connection, missing configuration, and invalid input failures.
- [ ] A ReadWrite API key is required for workflow use; the key never appears in ordinary output or errors.
- [ ] TOML, environment, and flag precedence is demonstrated at the packaged command boundary.
- [ ] Requests have a configurable per-request timeout with a 30-second default; timeout errors have a stable JSON shape and exit code.
- [ ] A controllable HTTP fixture verifies observable JSON, exit status, and requests without prompts.
notes: Package, profile precedence, version/authentication, timeout, redaction, and fixture tests pass. Live slskd 0.26.1.0 check/Search/Candidate/expiry passed with a separate configured ReadWrite key; profile and slskd key role were matched locally without printing the secret. The slskd API does not expose current key role, so check reports apiKeyRole:unverified and documentation requires operator verification.
close_reason: Connection workflow validated against local slskd with a configured ReadWrite key; upstream role introspection limit is explicit in JSON and docs.

title: Spec: agent-first slskd CLI workflows
description:
## Problem Statement

An agent needs to discover content and complete downloads through one trusted local slskd instance. Direct API scripting leaves connection setup, candidate inspection, mutation safety, timeout handling, and transfer observation to each caller. That makes workflows hard to compose and retry reliably. There is no implementation yet; the domain glossary and architectural decisions define the intended behavior.

## Solution

Provide an agent-first command-line interface distributed as a Node.js/TypeScript npm package exposing slskd-cli. The CLI connects to one configured slskd instance, checks compatibility, creates a bounded Search from a literal Search query, returns inspectable Candidates, enqueues only a Candidate explicitly selected by the calling agent, and reports slskd Transfer state until completion. Commands produce deterministic machine-readable JSON and stable exit codes, require literal acknowledgement for each State-changing command, and never maintain a separate Workflow state database.

## User Stories

1. As a calling agent, I want to configure one Connection profile, so that each command reaches the intended slskd instance.
2. As a calling agent, I want to supply connection settings through environment variables, so that automation can override the local profile.
3. As a calling agent, I want to supply connection settings through command-line flags, so that a one-off command can override the environment.
4. As a trusted user, I want the API key kept out of ordinary output and errors, so that automation logs do not expose it.
5. As a calling agent, I want an explicit connection or authentication error, so that I can correct the profile.
6. As a calling agent, I want a compatibility check for slskd 0.26.1 or later, so that workflows fail clearly against unsupported instances.
7. As a calling agent, I want a Search created from my literal Search query, so that the CLI does not silently reinterpret my intent.
8. As a calling agent, I want a Search identifier returned, so that I can retrieve its Candidates later.
9. As a calling agent, I want a configurable bounded Search lifetime with a 60-second default, so that results reflect current availability.
10. As a calling agent, I want an Expired search rejected clearly, so that I create a fresh Search.
11. As a calling agent, I want Candidates associated with their Search identifier, so that I know which Search produced them.
12. As a calling agent, I want a Candidate identifier for each Candidate, so that I can select one without reconstructing a peer path.
13. As a calling agent, I want Candidate metadata including source username and remote path, so that I can assess provenance.
14. As a calling agent, I want Candidate metadata including filename, extension, and byte size, so that I can assess whether a file fits my request.
15. As a calling agent, I want available queue or slot information, so that I can assess likely availability.
16. As a calling agent, I want available parsed audio attributes, so that I can assess format and quality when slskd exposes them.
17. As a calling agent, I want missing metadata represented explicitly, so that I do not mistake absence for a valid value.
18. As a calling agent, I want to inspect Candidates before enqueuing, so that selection stays under my control.
19. As a calling agent, I want to enqueue a Candidate using its Search and Candidate identifiers, so that the requested Transfer targets the inspected result.
20. As a calling agent, I want invalid, stale, or mismatched Candidate references rejected, so that I cannot enqueue an unintended file.
21. As a calling agent, I want a literal --yes on each State-changing command, so that mutations are intentional and non-interactive.
22. As a calling agent, I want a safely retried enqueue to report an existing matching Transfer, so that retries do not create duplicate downloads.
23. As a calling agent, I want an Ambiguous mutation reported as such, so that I can reconcile Transfer state before retrying.
24. As a calling agent, I want to inspect Transfer state, so that I can observe queueing, progress, failure, and completion.
25. As a calling agent, I want slskd's completed Transfer status to be the Workflow completion authority, so that I can resume observation without a CLI run database.
26. As a calling agent, I want to know the Transfer destination reported by slskd, so that I can find the downloaded file.
27. As a calling agent, I want cancellation to be idempotent for a completed or already-cancelled Transfer, so that retries converge on an inactive state.
28. As a calling agent, I want clearing or deleting a Transfer to require its own --yes, so that destructive actions are explicit.
29. As a calling agent, I want per-request timeouts with a 30-second default, so that an unresponsive instance cannot hang a workflow indefinitely.
30. As a calling agent, I want typed errors and stable exit codes, so that automation can distinguish invalid input, connection failure, incompatibility, timeout, and ambiguous mutation.
31. As a calling agent, I want deterministic JSON for successful commands and errors, so that I can parse results without terminal-oriented text.
32. As a calling agent, I want commands to run without prompts, so that workflows can operate unattended.
33. As a trusted user, I want the CLI to leave download placement and file deletion to slskd, so that the configured Transfer destination remains authoritative.
34. As a trusted user, I want a documented npm installation and executable, so that I can run the CLI on a supported Node.js LTS release.
35. As a calling agent, I want documented command examples and result shapes, so that I can assemble and recover a Workflow.

## Implementation Decisions

- Implement the CLI in TypeScript for a supported Node.js LTS release, with npm distribution and the slskd-cli executable. The current implementation issue calls out Node.js 24+; packaging must state the exact supported range.
- Treat one trusted local slskd instance as the only Search and Transfer state authority. The CLI stores only the narrow Connection profile; it does not create a Workflow-run database, persist Candidate caches, or manage downloaded files.
- Resolve Connection profile values in this order: local TOML profile, environment variables, then command-line flags. Report missing or invalid configuration without revealing the API key.
- Require a ReadWrite API key. Check configured slskd compatibility with version 0.26.1 or later before Workflow commands. Distinguish incompatibility from transport and authentication failures.
- Build command surfaces for configuration/compatibility, Search creation and Candidate inspection, Transfer enqueue and inspection, and Transfer cancellation/clearing/deletion. Keep command execution non-interactive.
- Pass each Search query as a single literal free-text string. Do not rewrite it, infer filters, rank Candidates, or choose one automatically.
- Return a Search identifier and opaque Candidate identifiers scoped to that Search. Validate their association and Search lifetime before enqueue. The default lifetime is 60 seconds and any override remains bounded.
- Normalize Candidate metadata at the CLI boundary. Include the fields named in the glossary and represent unavailable parsed attributes without invented values.
- Enqueue only the explicitly selected Candidate after a literal --yes. Before a retry creates a Transfer, reconcile matching slskd Transfer state and return an existing match when safe. Never automatically retry a mutation whose network outcome is unknown; return a typed Ambiguous mutation for the caller to reconcile.
- Read Transfer status from slskd. Report its destination and terminal state. Treat a completed Transfer as complete without claiming local file verification.
- Make cancellation idempotent for completed or already-cancelled Transfers. Require a fresh literal --yes for cancellation, clearing, and deletion.
- Apply a per-request timeout, defaulting to 30 seconds. Map invalid input, missing configuration, authentication, incompatibility, expired Search, missing Candidate, remote failure, timeout, and ambiguous mutation to stable JSON error shapes and exit codes. Keep success output deterministic.
- Document installation, Connection profile precedence, command contracts, JSON results, exit codes, acknowledgement rules, Search expiry, safe retry/reconciliation, and the limits of Transfer completion.
- Define precise command names, JSON fields, exit-code numbers, and environment-variable names as part of implementation before release; preserve their documented public contract once shipped.

## Testing Decisions

- Primary seam: execute the packaged CLI command boundary against a controllable slskd HTTP fixture. Assert observable JSON, exit status, and requests to the fixture; avoid tests coupled to internal helpers or module structure.
- Cover configuration precedence and redaction, compatibility and authentication failures, literal Search query handling, Candidate metadata and Search expiry, explicit Candidate selection, --yes enforcement, enqueue retry reconciliation, ambiguous mutation, Transfer observation and completion, idempotent cancellation, destructive Transfer commands, and request timeout.
- Include one representative end-to-end Workflow through the CLI seam: create Search, inspect Candidates, explicitly enqueue one, observe Transfer completion, and resume observation in a separate process without local Workflow state.
- Exercise the npm executable packaging and documented Node.js version as a release gate.
- There are no existing application tests or implementation seams yet. The CLI process boundary is the highest useful seam and supplies the initial prior art for later command tests. Add narrower tests only when a behavior cannot be tested reliably at that boundary.

## Out of Scope

- Automatic Candidate ranking or selection; query rewriting or a search DSL.
- A CLI-owned Workflow-run database, history, or resume token.
- Managing slskd's Transfer destination, moving or deleting downloaded files, or verifying local file contents.
- Multiple slskd instances, remote control-plane features, or Administrator-only functions.
- Media tagging, transcoding, library organization, and recommendation features.

## Further Notes

- This spec synthesizes the current glossary, the slskd-owns-workflow-state ADR, the Node.js/TypeScript/npm ADR, and the existing implementation issue.
- Work may be split into implementation children under this epic. The existing implementation issue should remain the tracked delivery item until more granular work is needed.
- The local Beads Dolt database is the issue source of truth. No remote sync is configured.
notes: 2026-10-17: User accepted destination:null for slskd 0.26.1 as the documented limitation. All other implementation and package checks passed; this resolves the remaining scope gap.
close_reason: All scoped CLI work complete; user accepted documented slskd 0.26.1 destination limitation.

title: Implement agent-first slskd CLI
description: Build the Node.js 24+ TypeScript npm CLI defined by the agreed domain model: a thin agent-first interface to one slskd 0.26.1+ instance, with deterministic JSON output, explicit candidate selection, safe mutations, bounded operations, and no local workflow state.
notes: CLI and docs implemented, fixture tests pass (8), package gate passes, live slskd 0.26.1.0 check/Search/Candidates/expiry pass with a dedicated ReadWrite key. Remaining epic gap is .5: upstream Transfer API lacks actual resolved destination; live instance has zero Transfers to inspect. No commit or remote sync under conservative repo policy.
close_reason: Agent-first CLI implemented, packaged, documented, and validated.

title: Report existing Transfer after concurrent enqueue conflict
description: Follow-up from the slskd-cli-9ps code review. In src/enqueue.ts a deterministic batch conflict (HTTP 409) reconciles the winning batch or Transfer but returns existing:false. A concurrent retry must distinguish a Transfer it found from one it created. Cover the 409 path through the packaged CLI fixture.
acceptance_criteria: When batch creation returns 409 and the matching Transfer is found, output has existing:true and no second Transfer is created; first creation still reports existing:false.

title: Configure oxlint and oxfmt
description: Add oxlint and oxfmt to the project in an isolated worktree, configure package scripts and tool settings, and validate linting and formatting without disturbing the existing dirty main worktree.
acceptance_criteria: Both oxlint and oxfmt are installed and configured; package scripts work; relevant checks pass or remaining violations are documented.

title: Define slskd CLI domain model
description: Capture settled terminology and architecture decisions while designing the agent-first command-line utility for slskd workflows.
close_reason: Completed the shared domain model and documented the accepted thin-client architecture.

title: Configure engineering skills
description: Configure the repository-facing issue tracker, triage label vocabulary, and domain documentation layout for the engineering skills.
close_reason: Configured Beads issue tracking, default triage labels, and single-context domain documentation guidance for engineering skills.

title: Unify Transfer state and terminal mapping
description: Design cleanup from the slskd-cli-9ps code review. src/transfer.ts separately computes terminal and status from overlapping state-string lists, which can drift when states are added. Centralize the state mapping while preserving the documented JSON contract.
acceptance_criteria: One mapping determines both normalized status and terminal; packaged CLI tests cover queued, active, succeeded, errored, and cancelled states without changing output.

title: Share unknown JSON object guard across Search and Transfer
description: Design cleanup from the slskd-cli-9ps code review. src/search.ts and src/transfer.ts repeat the same unknown-to-object guard. Evaluate a small shared helper to remove the duplication without coupling unrelated domain behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Duplicate object-guard logic is removed or a documented rationale explains why separate guards are preferable; typecheck and packaged CLI tests pass.
